keyVerseText: And Pharaohnechoh made Eliakim the son of Josiah king in the room of Josiah his father, and turned his name to Jehoiakim, and took Jehoahaz away: and he came to Egypt, and died there.
rootMeaning: The name יְהוֹיָקִים (Jehoiakim) derives from the Hebrew root combining יְהֹוָה (Jehovah), the personal name of God, with the verb קוּם meaning 'to raise' or 'to establish.' Thus, the literal meaning is 'Jehovah will raise up' or 'Jehovah establishes.' This etymology highlights the divine initiative and sovereignty behind the name, emphasizing that it is God who raises and sustains leaders. Such a root meaning carries more depth than the mere English transliteration, pointing to a foundational trust in God's providential power.
usageInScripture: The word יְהוֹיָקִים appears 37 times in the Hebrew Bible, predominantly as a proper name referring to the king of Judah, son of Josiah. The majority of its translations focus on identifying the person—'of Jehoiakim' and 'Jehoiakim'—which underscores its function as a personal name rather than a common noun. The consistent use of the name in various narrative contexts, including historical and prophetic texts, reveals its importance in the biblical record as a figure whose reign and actions are significant to the unfolding story of Judah and God's dealings with His people.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding the meaning of יְהוֹיָקִים as 'Jehovah raises up' invites reflection on God's sovereign role in appointing leaders, even those who may fail or fall away. The fact that Jehoiakim was a king under God's providence, yet subject to judgment and a violent end, reminds believers that God's authority transcends human authority. This name also points forward to the necessity of divine raising and sustaining, fulfilled ultimately in Christ, who is God's appointed King and Savior. The tension between God's sovereign raising of Jehoiakim and the king's personal failures encourages faith in God's unchanging power to establish His purposes despite human frailty.
keyVerseReflection: In 2 Kings 23:34, Pharaohnechoh installs Eliakim, son of Josiah, as king and changes his name to Jehoiakim, signaling a new divine appointment under foreign authority. The name change to יְהוֹיָקִים (Jehovah establishes) reflects God's sovereign role in raising him up even amid political upheaval. This verse highlights the theological significance of the name, showing that despite human political machinations, it is ultimately Jehovah who raises and sets up kings according to His will.
